Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

(p-323) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah Sad

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder.﴾ The majority of reciters, including the seven readers, read ص (Sad) with sukun (ص). The verified view is that ص is one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginnings of surahs, like ص in His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad.﴾ and His saying: ﴿Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad.﴾ [Maryam: 1].

We have already discussed the disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs in full at the beginning of Surah Hud, so there is no need to repeat it here.

By the verified view mentioned, you know that the readings of those who read ص with a kasrah on the dal without tanwin, those who read it with a kasrah on the dal with tanwin, those who read it with a fatha on the dal, and those who read it with a damma on the dal without tanwin, are all irregular (shadhdhah) readings on which no reliance is placed.

Likewise, the tafsirs of some scholars that are built upon those readings are not relied upon either.

It has been narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "Sad with a kasrah on the dal is an imperative verb from sada, yusadi, musadat, meaning to respond or oppose (ʿāraḍa), and from it comes al-sada (echo). It is what returns the sound in hard places empty of bodies. That is: oppose the Qur'an with your deeds, confront it with them, meaning comply with its commands, avoid its prohibitions, hold its creeds, take lessons from its examples, and be admonished by its admonitions."

Also from al-Hasan: "Sad means 'occurrence' (ḥādith), which is close to the first."

The reading of ص with a kasrah on the dal without tanwin is related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu al-Simal, Ibn Abi 'Aylah, and Nasr ibn 'Asim.

The most apparent explanation of this irregular reading is that the kasrah on the dal was due to lightening because of the meeting of two sukuns, and the letter is a letter of spelling (huruf hijaʾ), not an imperative verb from sada.

In a narration from Ibn Abi Ishaq, he read ص with a kasrah on the dal with tanwin, taking it as (p-324) genitive by an omitted oath particle. This, as you see, is clearly weak.

Likewise the reading of those who read ص with a fatha on the dal without tanwin is an irregular reading, and the tafsirs built upon it are baseless.

As in the saying of one who said: "Sada Muhammad the hearts of people and won them over until they believed in him."

And the saying of one who said: "It is in the accusative by way of incitement (al-ighra'), meaning hold fast to Sad," that is, this surah. And the saying of one who said its meaning is "recite." And the saying of one who said: it is in the accusative by removing the preposition, which is the omitted oath particle.

The closest of these views on these irregular readings is that the dal was given a fatha for lightening because of the meeting of two sukuns, and the fatha was chosen to match the sad (ṣād), and because fatha is the lightest of the vowels. This reading is the reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, and is narrated from Mahbub from Abu 'Amr.

Likewise the reading of one who read صادُ with a damma on the dal without tanwin, taking it as a proper name for the surah, and as the predicate of an omitted subject, the estimate being "this is Sadu," and that it is prevented from diptotic declension (ṣarf) because of definiteness as a proper noun and feminine gender, since the surah is feminine in form.

This reading is related from al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn al-Sumayqa, and Harun al-A'war.

Whoever reads صادَ with a fatha on the dal reads ق and ن similarly. And likewise whoever reads ص with a damma on the dal reads ق as و ن with a damma on the fa' and the nun.

The summary is that all these readings, and all these tafsirs built upon them, are entirely baseless, with no reliance placed upon them.

We have only mentioned them to draw attention to this.

There is no doubt that the verified view is what we have presented, that ص is one of the disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs, and that the reading from which one may not deviate is the reading of the majority that we have mentioned.

Some scholars have said: ص is the key to some of the names of Allah, may He be exalted, such as al-Sabur and al-Samad.

Some of them said its meaning is: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth in what he conveys from Allah," and other views (p-325) among those.

We have mentioned that we have already discussed this in full at the beginning of Surah Hud.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿By the Qur'an, full of reminder.﴾ We have already mentioned that the original form of al-Qur'an is a verbal noun (maṣdar) to which the alif and nun were added, as they were added in al-ṭughyān (transgression), al-rujḥān (preponderance), al-kufrān (disbelief), and al-khusrān (loss), and that this verbal noun is intended as a description.

Most scholars say that this description expressed by the verbal noun is the passive participle (ism al-maf'ūl).

On this basis, al-Qur'an means "the thing recited," from the Arabs' saying: qara'tu al-shay' ("I read the thing") when I make it apparent and bring it out. From it comes: qara'at al-nāqah al-salā wa al-janīn ("the she-camel expelled the afterbirth and the fetus") when she brings it out and displays it from her belly. From it is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm in his Mu'allaqah:

"She shows you, when you enter upon the sheltered place, while the eyes of the enviers are secure,
The two forearms of a long-necked, white-skinned, young she-camel, of pure white color, whom the womb had not yet hidden (qara'at)."

According to one of the two narrations of the verse.

The meaning of al-Qur'an on this basis is the thing recited, which the reciter makes apparent and brings out from his mouth with its clear expressions.

Some scholars said: the description expressed by the verbal noun is the active participle (ism al-fā'il).

On this basis, al-Qur'an means "the reciter," an active participle of qara'tu meaning "I gathered."

From it is the Arabs' saying: qara'tu al-mā' fī al-ḥawḍ, meaning I gathered the water in the basin.

On this basis, al-Qur'an means "the reciter," that is, "the gatherer," because Allah gathered in it everything in the revealed books.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿full of reminder﴾ has two well-known explanations among scholars.

The first: that dhikr means honor (sharaf). The Arabs say: "So-and-so is mentioned," meaning he has a reputation, that is, honor.

(p-326) From it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and your people.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44], meaning an honor for you, according to one of the two views.

The second: that dhikr is a verbal noun meaning admonition (tadhkīr), because the great Qur'an contains admonition and exhortations. This is the view of the majority, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

Note

Know that scholars differed in determining what Allah swore by in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the Qur'an, full of reminder.﴾ Some said the thing sworn to is mentioned. Those who said it is mentioned differed in specifying it, and all their views on this are manifestly baseless.

Among them are those who said the thing sworn to is His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is true: the quarreling of the people of the Fire.﴾ [Sad: 64].

And among them are those who said it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end.﴾ [Sad: 54].

And among them are those who said it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is none but that he denied the messengers, so My punishment was due.﴾ [Sad: 14], like His saying: ﴿By Allah, we were indeed in clear error.﴾ And His saying: ﴿By the sky and the night-comer. And what will make you know what the night-comer is? The piercing star. There is no soul but that it has over it a guardian.﴾ [al-Tariq: 1-4].

And among them are those who said it is His saying: ﴿How many generations have We destroyed before them?﴾. Whoever says this says: the original is "la-kam ahlaknā" (how many We have destroyed), and when the speech became long, the lam of the oath was omitted, so it said: "kam ahlaknā" without the lam.

They said: a parallel to this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the sun and its brightness.﴾ [al-Shams: 1], for when the speech became long between the oath and the thing sworn to, which is ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it.﴾, the lam of the oath was omitted from it.

And among them are those who said the thing sworn to is His saying: "Sad." They said the meaning of Sad is "The Messenger of Allah spoke the truth," and "By the Qur'an, full of reminder." On this basis, the thing sworn to is his truthfulness (ﷺ).

And among them are those who said the meaning is: "This is Sad," that is, the surah that overcame the Arabs, "By the Qur'an, full of reminder," and other views whose baselessness is not hidden.

Some scholars said the thing sworn to is omitted, and they differed in estimating it. Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: the estimate is "By the Qur'an, full of reminder, indeed it is miraculous (p-327)." Ibn 'Atiyyah and others estimated it, saying: "By the Qur'an, full of reminder, the matter is not as the disbelievers say," and other views.

The one who wrote this, may Allah pardon and forgive him, says: What appears correct, by the evidence of inductive study of the Qur'an, is that the answer to the oath is omitted, and that its estimate is: "By the Qur'an, full of reminder, the matter is not as the disbelievers say." The thing negated by the oath includes three mutually connected matters.

The first: that the Prophet (ﷺ) is truly sent by Allah, and that the matter is not as the disbelievers say, as in His saying about them: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger."﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43].

The second: that the true God who is worshipped, may He be exalted, is One, and that the matter is not as the disbelievers say, as in His saying about them: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing.﴾ [Sad: 5].

The third: that Allah, may He be exalted, resurrects those who die, and that the matter is not as the disbelievers say, as in His saying about them: ﴿And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die.﴾ [al-Nahl: 38].
• And His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected.﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7].
• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us."﴾ [Saba': 3].

As for the evidence from the Qur'an that the thing negated is omitted, it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition.﴾ [Sad: 2]; for the turning away (idrab) by His saying "bal" (but) is clear evidence of the omitted thing sworn to. That is: the matter is not as those who disbelieve say; rather, those who disbelieve are in arrogance, that is, in zealotry, pride, and haughtiness against the truth, and in opposition, that is, in defiance and obstinacy.

As for the indication of the inductive study of the Qur'an that the omitted negated thing includes the three matters mentioned, it is by the indication of many verses. As for the validity of the Messenger's message (ﷺ), and that the true God who is worshipped has no partner, He has pointed to both here.

As for the Messenger being truly sent, it is in His saying here: ﴿And they wondered that a warner from among themselves has come to them, and the disbelievers said, "This is a magician, a liar."﴾ [Sad: 4], meaning: there is no reason for the mentioned wonder that a warner from among them should come.

There is no doubt that he came by a true sending from Allah.

(p-328) And their saying: ﴿This is a magician, a liar.﴾ Allah mentioned it only as a rejection of them and a denial of them. Thus it is known that within the meaning of "By the Qur'an, full of reminder" is that you are truly a messenger, even though they wondered at your coming as a warner to them, and claimed that you are a magician, a liar. That is, it is they who wondered at the truth about which there is no doubt, and claimed that the seal of the messengers, the most honored of them before Allah, is a magician and a liar.

As for the true God who is worshipped having no partner, it is in His saying here: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing.﴾ [Sad: 5]; for the interrogative hamza in His saying "a-ja'ala" is for denial, containing the meaning of negation, so it indicates the negation of the cause of their wonder at his saying (ﷺ): that the true God who is worshipped is One.

These two matters are also indicated by other verses of the great Qur'an, in which Allah swore to their falsity and to their affirmation explicitly by oath. Such as His saying, may He be exalted, swearing that the Messenger is truly sent: ﴿Ya Sin. By the wise Qur'an. Indeed, you are among the messengers.﴾ [Ya Sin: 1-3]. These clarify the meaning of "Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder": that you are among the messengers.

The affirmation of the validity of that message has come in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 252].

As for His being the true God worshipped with no partner, He, may He be exalted, has sworn to it in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By those who line up in rows. And by those who drive away with a driving. And by those who recite the reminder. Indeed, your God is One.﴾ [al-Saffat: 1-4], and other such verses. This indicates that the meaning includes what is mentioned, namely: "By the Qur'an, full of reminder, indeed your God is One," as He indicated by His saying: ﴿Has he made the gods...﴾ the verse [Sad: 5].

As for the resurrection being true, He has sworn to it with a valid, explicit oath in verses of the Book of Allah:
• Such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected."﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7].
• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾ [al-Taghabun: 3], that is, the Hour.
• And His saying: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true."﴾ [Yunus: 53].

He swore by two of the three things mentioned, and omitted the object of the oath, which is the two things mentioned: that the Messenger is sent, and that resurrection is true. He indicated this clearly in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an!﴾ ﴿But they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing!"﴾ ﴿"When we have died and become dust? That is a far-off return."﴾ [Qaf: 1-3]. Thus it becomes clear (p-329) that the meaning is: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an!﴾, that the warner who is from among you, at whose coming you wondered, is a warner sent to you by Allah in truth, and that the resurrection which you denied and deemed far-fetched, with the utmost denial and deeming it remote, in His saying, exalted is He, about you: ﴿"When we have died and become dust? That is a far-off return."﴾, that is, that return which is resurrection is, in your claim, a far-off return, yet it is certain to occur without doubt, and it is true beyond any doubt, as He indicated in His saying: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record.﴾ The meaning is that what the earth has consumed of their flesh, and what it has scattered of their bodies and bones, is known to Him, exalted and high; nothing of it is hidden from Him, so He is able to return it as it was.

And the revival of those decayed bodies, those scattered hairs and crumbling bones, as we have already explained with clear Qur'anic verses in Surah Ya-Sin, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And the Horn is blown, and behold, they rush forth from the graves to their Lord﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51]. And the fact that he (ﷺ) is truly sent from Allah necessarily implies, beyond any doubt, that the Great Qur'an is truly sent down from Allah, and that it is not sorcery, nor poetry, nor soothsaying, nor "the fables of the ancients."

For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, swore in many places that the Qur'an is also sent down from Allah, such as His saying at the beginning of Surah ad-Dukhan: ﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ ﴿By the clear Book!﴾ ﴿Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 1-3], and His saying at the beginning of Surah az-Zukhruf: ﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ ﴿By the clear Book!﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand.﴾ ﴿And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 1-4].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, but those who disbelieve are in arrogance and dissension﴾. We have already discussed earlier, in some detail, the use of "bal" (nay, but) for a turning away from what precedes in this verse.

His saying, may He be exalted, here: ﴿in arrogance﴾ means: in zealous pride and haughtiness when accepting the truth. Exalted is He, in Surat al-Baqarah He made clear that among the causes of the arrogance mentioned being taken up with sin by the disbelievers is their being commanded to fear Allah. He also made clear that this arrogance, which is zealous pride and haughtiness against accepting the truth, is among the causes of their entering Hell. This is in His saying about some of the disbelievers who show other than what they conceal: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," arrogance takes him up in sin. For him, Hell is sufficient, and surely it is an evil resting place﴾ [al-Baqarah: 206].

The apparent reason for applying the word "izzah" (might, arrogance) to zealous pride and haughtiness is that whoever is characterized by it places himself in the position of one who overpowers and dominates, even though the matter is not so. This is because the original meaning of "izzah" in the language of the Arabs is dominance and subjugation. From it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], and the Arabs say: "Man 'azeez" (who is mighty), meaning whoever prevails and plunders. From it is the saying of al-Khansa':

"As if they had never been a protected sanctuary, when people, at that time, were overpowered."

And His saying, may He be exalted, about the litigants who scaled the wall to reach Dawud: ﴿and he overpowered me in the speech﴾ [Sad: 23], meaning he overcame me and subdued me in the dispute.

The evidence from the Qur'an that the "izzah" which Allah ascribed to the disbelievers in His saying, ﴿Nay, but those who disbelieve are in arrogance﴾, and His saying, ﴿arrogance takes him up in sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 206], is not the "izzah" that is meant as actual domination and overpowering, is that Allah restricted this "izzah" to the believers rather than the disbelievers and hypocrites, in His saying: ﴿They say, "If we return to Madinah, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble." And might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

For this reason, the scholars of tafsir interpreted it as zealous pride and haughtiness against accepting the truth.

As for "shiqaq" (dissension), it means opposition and obstinate hostility, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if they turn away, they are only in dissension﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137]. Some scholars said: its root is from "shiqq" (side), because the opponent and obstinate one is on a side, that is, on the side where there is no one who opposes him and is obstinate toward him.

Some people of knowledge said: the root of "shiqaq" is from "mashaqqah" (hardship), because the opponent and obstinate one strives to bring hardship upon whoever is opposed and obstinately resisted.

Some of them said: the root of "shiqaq" is from "shaqq al-'asa" (splitting the staff), which is discord and division.

[p-331] The Almighty's saying: ﴿How many generations did We destroy before them, and they cried out when there was no longer any escape.﴾ *Kam* here is the informative (*khabariyyah*) *kam*, meaning it informs of a great number. It is in the accusative position, functioning as the direct object of *ahlakna* ("We destroyed"). The plural form in *ahlakna* is for magnification. The *min* in His saying *min qarn* ("from a generation") is a specifying *min* (*mumayyizah*) for *kam*. *Al-qarn* is applied to a nation and also to a period of time, and the most well-known opinion about it is that it is a hundred years. The meaning is: We destroyed many of the past nations because of disbelief and their denial of the Messengers. [p-331] Therefore, O disbelievers of Makkah, beware of denying our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and of disbelieving in what he brought, lest We destroy you on account of that, as We destroyed the many generations of the past with it.

The Almighty has mentioned three matters in this noble verse:

The first: that He destroyed many generations of the past, threatening the disbelievers of Makkah with that.

The second: that they cried out, meaning when they witnessed the first signs of destruction.

The third: that this time, which is the time of witnessing the punishment, is not a time for crying out. That is, it is a time in which there is no refuge, and no escape from destruction after it has been witnessed.

The Almighty has explained these three matters mentioned here in many verses of His Book.

As for the first matter, that He destroyed many nations, He mentioned it in many verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And how many generations We destroyed after Noah﴾ [al-Isra: 17].

• His saying: ﴿How many a town We destroyed while it was wrongdoing﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Hajj: 45].

• His saying: ﴿Has there not reached you the news of those before you, the people of Noah, and 'Ad and Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows but Allah?﴾, to the end of the verse [Ibrahim: 9].

The verses of this kind are many.

The Almighty has also mentioned in many verses that the cause of the destruction of those nations was disbelief in Allah and the denial of His Messengers, as in His saying in this last verse, explaining the cause of the destruction of those nations, which He identified: ﴿Whom none knows but Allah. Their Messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said, "We disbelieve in what you have been sent with, and we are truly in grave doubt about that to which you invite us."﴾ [Ibrahim: 9].

We have already discussed, in our commentary on this verse of Surah Ibrahim, the opinions of scholars regarding His saying ﴿they put their hands to their mouths﴾, and we explained the indication of the Qur'an concerning some of them.

• And as in His saying: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His Messengers, so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment. So it tasted the consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 8-9].

• And His saying: ﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the Messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and 'Ad and Thamud and the companions of the Rass, and generations between them, many﴾ ﴿and to each We presented examples, and each We utterly destroyed﴾ [al-Furqan: 37-39].

• And His saying: ﴿There was not one but denied the Messengers, so My punishment was justly due﴾ [Sad: 14].

• And His saying: ﴿Each denied the Messengers, so My warning came due﴾ [Qaf: 14].

The verses of this kind are many.

The Almighty has explained that the purpose of mentioning the destruction of the past nations because of disbelief and the denial of the Messengers is to threaten and frighten the disbelievers of Makkah, lest there befall them the like of what befell those, if they persist in disbelief and in denying him (ﷺ).

He mentioned this in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿Have they not travelled in the land and seen what was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers is the like of it﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. For His saying ﴿and for the disbelievers is the like of it﴾ is a great threat in this regard.

And His saying: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of hard clay, layered, marked from your Lord. And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud: 82-83]. His saying ﴿and it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ contains a great threat to whoever does the deed of the people of Lot, of disbelief and denial of their prophet, and of their well-known abominations. The Almighty has also rebuked whoever does not take warning from them and does not fear that the like of what befell them may befall him, as in His saying about the people of Lot: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ ﴿and at night. Will you not reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138]. And His saying: ﴿They had certainly passed by the town which was rained upon with a rain of evil. Did they not see it? Rather, they did not expect resurrection﴾ [al-Furqan: 40].

• And His saying about them: ﴿And We have left of it a clear sign for a people who reason﴾ [al-Ankabut: 35].

• And His saying about them: ﴿And indeed it is on a road that remains﴾.

• And His saying about them and about the people of Shu'ayb: ﴿And indeed both are on a clear highway﴾ [al-Hijr: 79].

The verses of this kind are many.

As for the second matter, which is their crying out when they perceive the first signs of the punishment, the Almighty has mentioned in verses of His Book two kinds of that crying out:

One of them: their crying out by acknowledging that they were wrongdoers. This is in His saying: ﴿And how many a town We shattered which had been wrongdoing, and We brought into being after it another people﴾ ﴿And when they perceived Our might, there they were, fleeing from it﴾, up to His saying ﴿They said, "O woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿And that remained their cry until We made them as cut grain, extinguished﴾ [al-Anbiya: 11-15]. And His saying: ﴿And how many a town We destroyed, and Our punishment came to it by night or while they were napping﴾ ﴿And their cry, when Our punishment came to them, was only that they said, "Indeed we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 4-5].

The second: of the two kinds of crying out mentioned, their crying out by believing in Allah, seeking relief from that punishment whose first signs they perceived, as in His saying: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ ﴿But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the established way of Allah regarding His servants, and there the disbelievers lost﴾ [Ghafir: 84-85]. This last kind is the more suitable and fitting to the context, because of the indication of His saying: ﴿and there was no longer any escape﴾ concerning it.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and there was no longer any escape﴾, which is the third matter, its meaning is: it is not the time in which they cried out, which is the time of witnessing the punishment, "when there is no escape", that is, it is not a time of flight, nor a refuge from that punishment which they witnessed.

So His saying *wala* ("and not") is *la* of negation, to which the feminine suffix of pronunciation (*ta' al-ta'nith al-lafziyyah*) has been added, just as it was added in *thamma* (there), so it is said *thammat*, and in *rubba* (perhaps), so it is said *rubbat*.

The most prominent opinions of the grammarians (*al-nahwiyyun*) about it are that it works in the manner of *laysa* ("is not"), and that it does not work except on *hin* (time) specifically, or on the word *hin* and similar times, such as *al-sa'ah* (the hour) and *al-awan* (the moment). It is also said that its subject or its predicate must be omitted, and most often the nominative of the two is omitted while the accusative is retained; sometimes this is reversed. This is the view of Sibawayh, and Ibn Malik (d. 672 AH) alluded to it in *al-Khulasah* with his saying:

"In indefinites, *la* is made to work like *laysa*, and it may follow *lata* and *in*, which also work."

"The work of *lata* is only in *hin*, and the omission of the nominative is widespread, while the reverse is rare."

The word *manas* is a noun of place (*maf'al*) from *al-nawS* (retreat), and the Arabs say: *nasahu yanusuhu* when he escaped it and was unable to reach it. *Al-manas* is also applied to delay, because whoever delays and turns toward a refuge that saves him from what he feared has found *manas*.

*Al-manas*, *al-malja'*, *al-mafarr*, and *al-mawil* all have one meaning. The Arabs say: *istanasa*, meaning he sought *manas*, that is, safety and an escape from what he feared. From this is the saying of Harithah ibn Badr:

"A man of deep strength, when I hold back his rein, with my hand he seeks escape and wants the running of the mule-like mount."

The more apparent view is that the application of *al-nawS* to escape and advancement, and its application to delay and evasion, both refer back to one thing. This is because *al-manas* is a mimi verbal noun whose meaning applies to its particulars: that its possessor is in distress and constraint, so he does a deed by which his deliverance and salvation from that are achieved.

[p-334] Sometimes that deed is by running and hastening ahead of whoever intends him harm, and sometimes it is by delay and evasion until he is saved from that.

The Arabs use *al-nawS* for delay, and *al-bawS* with the single-dotted *ba'* for advancement. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"From the remembrance of Salma, when she departed from you, moving back, falling short of her by a step, and advancing."

The most correct of the opinions about *lata* is that the *ta'* is separate from *hin*, and that it works in the manner of *laysa*, contrary to those who say it works in the manner of *inna*, and contrary to those who say the *ta'* is attached to *hin*, and that he saw it so in the *Imam*, which is the codex of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), in which it is attached to it.

According to the view of the majority, including the seven readers (*al-qurra' al-sab'ah*), that the *ta'* is not joined to *hin*, pausing on *lata* with the *ta'* is the practice of all of them, except al-Kisa'i, who pauses on it with the *ha'*.

As for the reading with a *kasrah* or a *dammah* on the *ta'*, both are irregular (*shadhdh*), and it is not permissible to recite with them. Likewise the reading with a *kasrah* on the *nun* of *hin* is irregular and not permissible, although explaining its meaning according to it is difficult.

Al-Zamakhshari (d. 538 AH) took a far-fetched view for it, the falseness of which is not hidden, and Abu Hayyan refuted him in *al-Bahr al-Muhit*. Abu Hayyan preferred that the explanation of the *kasrah* reading is that *hin* is in the genitive by an elided *min*.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and they cried out﴾, the origin of *al-nida'* (crying out) is raising the voice. The Arabs say: "So-and-so is more sonorous of voice than so-and-so," meaning louder. From this is his saying:

"I said, 'Call, and I will call, for indeed the more sonorous of two voices is the one who calls out.'"

What this noble verse contains, that the past destroyed nations cry out when they witness the punishment, and that this time is not a time for crying out, since there is no refuge in it, nor escape, nor *manas*, has been mentioned in other places as well, such as His saying: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ ﴿But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾, to the end of the verse [Ghafir: 84-85]. And His saying: ﴿And when they perceived Our might, there they were, fleeing from it﴾ ﴿"Do not flee, but return to what you were made to live in luxury and your dwellings; perhaps you will be questioned."﴾ ﴿They said, "O woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿And that remained their cry until We made them as cut grain, extinguished﴾ [al-Anbiya: 12-15], and other verses besides.

[p-335] The Almighty has also explained that the like of this occurs on the Day of Resurrection, in verses of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be turned back. You will have no refuge that Day, nor will you have any denial﴾ [al-Shura: 47]. And His saying: ﴿So when sight is dazzled﴾ ﴿and the moon is eclipsed﴾ ﴿and the sun and moon are joined﴾ ﴿Man will say that Day, "Where is the escape?"﴾ ﴿No! There is no refuge﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 7-11]. *Al-wazar* means refuge, and from it is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him):

"The people are a confederacy against us because of you; for us there is nothing but spear-points and the tips of lances as refuge."

And as in His saying: ﴿Rather, for them is a promise; they will not find besides it any *mawil*﴾ [al-Kahf: 58]. *Al-mawil* is a noun of place from *wa'ala ya'alu*, when one finds a refuge to take hold of. From it is the saying of al-A'sha, Maymun ibn Qays:

"And I may steal from the master of the house his heedlessness, and he may beware of me, yet he will not escape (*thumma ma yi'al*)."

That is: then he does not escape.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they wonder that a warner from among themselves has come to them﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the disbelievers of Quraysh wondered because a messenger, a warner from among them, had come to them. The wonder He mentions in this verse, He mentions elsewhere, rejects it, explains its cause, and refutes it in other verses. Regarding this wonder, He said: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an﴾ ﴿Nay, but they wonder that a warner from among themselves has come to them﴾ [Qaf: 1-2].

Allah also said, rejecting it, at the beginning of Surah Yunus: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the wise Book﴾ ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn mankind"?﴾ [Yunus: 1-2]. He mentioned a similar wonder in Surah al-A'raf concerning the people of Noah and the people of Hud. He said of Noah, addressing his people: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you, and that you may fear Allah and perhaps receive mercy?﴾ [al-A'raf: 63].

And He said of Hud, addressing 'Ad: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you? And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah...﴾ to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 69]. He made clear that the cause of their wonder at the warner being from among them was that he is a human like them, while they claimed that Allah does not send to them anyone of their own kind. And that if He wished to send someone to them, He would send an angel to them, because he is not a human like them, and he does not eat (p-336) or drink or walk in the markets.

The verses on this are many:

• Such as the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ ﴿Say: "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ [al-Isra: 94-95]

• And His words: ﴿Shall we believe two humans like us, when their people are worshippers of us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 47]

• And His words: ﴿The chiefs of his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had given luxury in the worldly life, said: "This is none but a human like you, who eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink." ﴾ ﴿"And if you obey a human like yourselves, then you will surely be losers."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 33-34]

• And His words: ﴿And they said: "What is this messenger who eats food and walks in the markets?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 7]

• And His words: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said: "Shall humans guide us?"﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Taghabun: 6].

• And His words: ﴿Thamud denied the warnings﴾ ﴿and said: "Shall we follow a single human from among us? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness."﴾ [al-Qamar: 23-24]

• And His words: ﴿They said: "You are only humans like us"﴾ to the end of the verse [Ibrahim: 10].

• And His words: ﴿And they said: "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved.﴾ ﴿And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered for them what they cover.﴾ [al-An'am: 8-9]

• And His words: ﴿But if they turn away, say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and behind them, saying: "Worship none but Allah." They said: "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels, so we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ [Fussilat: 13-14]

• And His words: ﴿So the chiefs of his people who disbelieved said: "This is none but a human like you, who wants to take superiority over you. And if Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels. We never heard of this among our forefathers of old."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 24]

• And His words: ﴿And they said: "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed, indeed you are mad!"﴾ ﴿"Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are of the truthful?"﴾ ﴿"We send not the angels except with truth, and then they would not be respited."﴾ [al-Hijr: 6-8]

• And His words: ﴿"Why has an angel not been sent down to him, so that he might be a warner with him?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 7]

• And His words: ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say: "Why have the angels not been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great transgression.﴾ ﴿On the day they see the angels, there will be no glad tidings that day for the criminals,﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Furqan: 21-22].

• And His words concerning Pharaoh with Moses: ﴿"Why have bracelets of gold not been put upon him, or the angels not come with him in procession?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 53].

Allah has refuted the disbelievers' wonder at the sending of messengers from among mankind in verses of His Book, (p-337)

• such as His words: ﴿We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20].

• And His words: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you and given them wives and offspring﴾ [al-Ra'd: 38].

• And His words: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109].

• And His words: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know.﴾ ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 7-8]

• And His words: ﴿Their messengers said to them: "We are only humans like you, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾ [Ibrahim: 11].

That is, with the messengership and the revelation, even if he were a human like you, and so on through the other verses.

The Exalted said: ﴿And the chiefs among them went off, [saying], "Walk on, and be steadfast in [the worship of] your gods."﴾ We have already discussed this verse in Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in [the worship of] them﴾ [al-Furqan: 42].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ In this noble verse, the Majestic and Exalted mentions that the disbelievers of Makkah denied that Allah had singled out His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to receive the Qur'an alone, and had not sent it down to anyone else among them. What this noble verse indicates has come in other verses, along with the refutation of the disbelievers in their denial of his (ﷺ) particular designation with revelation, such as His saying, the Exalted, about them: ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 31]. By "the two cities" they mean Makkah and al-Ta'if, and by "the two men from the two cities" they mean al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in Makkah and Urwah ibn Mas'ud in al-Ta'if, claiming that they were more deserving of prophethood than him.

Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, has refuted that claim of theirs in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 32]. This is because the interrogative hamzah in His saying "Is it they who distribute" is for denunciation, which carries the meaning of negation. Likewise is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We will not believe until we are given what the messengers of Allah were given."﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

Allah, the Exalted, has refuted that from them in His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message. Those who committed crime will be struck with humiliation before Allah and a severe punishment for what they used to plot﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. He also alluded to the refutation of that from them in this surah of Sad, in His saying: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder. Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment. Or do they have the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower? Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them?﴾ up to the verse [Sad: 8–10]. (p-338) This is because He does not place the message wherever He wills and single out whomever He wills with it except one who has the treasuries of mercy. And dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ He has clarified in another place that Thamud said the like of this to the Prophet of Allah Salih, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, and that is in His saying, the Exalted, about them: ﴿Has the Reminder been cast upon him from among us? Rather, he is a liar, an insolent one.﴾ [al-Qamar: 25]. Allah, the Exalted, has refuted that from them in His saying: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent one.﴾ [al-Qamar: 26].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do they possess the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them?﴾ We have already presented some discussion of this in Surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We guarded them from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and ʿĀd, and Pharaoh, owner of the stakes﴾ ﴿and Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the companions of the Thicket. Those are the confederates﴾ ﴿Each one of them denied the messengers, so My punishment was deserved﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they deny you, then before them the people of Noah denied﴾ [al-Hajj: 42], and in other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 16:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share [of punishment] before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify it in several places of this blessed Book: in Surat al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me.﴾ [al-An'am: 57]. And in Surat Yunus, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then, when it occurs, will you believe in it?﴾ and the verse [Yunus: 51]. And in Surat al-Ra'd, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they ask you to hasten evil before good﴾ and the verse [al-Ra'd: 6]. And in Surat al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾ and the verse [al-Hajj: 47].

We have already noted that al-qitt (a share of something, i.e., one's portion) means: hasten to us our share of the punishment with which You threaten us.

And the original meaning of al-qitt is the book of reward (kitab al-ja'izah), because the king writes in it the share that he gives to that person. Its plural is quttun. From it is the saying of al-A'sha:(p-339)

؎Nor the king al-Nu'man, when I meet him in his abundance, gives the quttu (writs of grants) and distinguishes [among them].

His saying "wa-ya'fiq" means: he favors some of them over others in the gift that is written in the quttu.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with him﴾ up to His saying: ﴿oft-returning﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah al-Anbiya', in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with David, and the birds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 79].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 21:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah Sad

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Has there come to you the news of the adversaries?﴾ — the verse.

This verse, by its apparent meaning, indicates that the word "khasm" (adversary) is singular, but the pronouns following it indicate otherwise.

The answer is that "khasm" originally is a verbal noun (masdar) of "khasamahu" (he disputed with him), and when the Arabs describe with a verbal noun, they use it in the singular and masculine form.

Accordingly, "al-khasm" may be meant to refer to a group, a single person, or two persons, and it is permissible to make it plural or dual, by forgetting its original root, which is the verbal noun, and treating it as a descriptive word (wasf).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And David realized that We had tried him, so he asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down prostrate, and turned in repentance.﴾ ﴿So We forgave him that.﴾ We have already presented the discussion on similar verses of the Qur'an, those from which it is understood that some lapse proceeded from the prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, and we clarified the statements of the scholars of usul (the foundations of jurisprudence) on this matter in surah Ta-Ha, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray﴾ [Ta-Ha: 121].

Know that what many of the exegetes mention in the interpretation of this noble verse, of things that are not befitting to the station of David, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayer and peace, all of it goes back to the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from the Israelite traditions), so there is no reliance upon it, and nothing is to be depended upon from it. And whatever has come from it traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), none of it is authentic.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا داوُدُ إنّا جَعَلْناكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الأرْضِ فاحْكُمْ بَيْنَ النّاسِ بِالحَقِّ ولا تَتَّبِعِ الهَوى فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾. قَوْلُهُ تَعالى فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْناكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الأرْضِ﴾، قَدْ بَيَّنّا الحُكْمَ الَّذِي دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ فِي سُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ، فِي الكَلامِ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ إنِّي جاعِلٌ فِي الأرْضِ خَلِيفَةً﴾ الآيَةَ [٢]. وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ: ﴿فاحْكُمْ بَيْنَ النّاسِ بِالحَقِّ ولا تَتَّبِعِ الهَوى فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ قَدْ أمَرَ فِيهِ نَبِيَّهُ داوُدَ بِالحُكْمِ بَيْنَ النّاسِ بِالحَقِّ، ونَهاهُ فِيهِ عَنِ اتِّباعِ الهَوى، وأنَّ اتِّباعَ الهَوى عِلَّةٌ لِلضَّلالِ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، لِأنَّ الفاءَ فِي قَوْلِهِ ﴿فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ تَدُلُّ عَلى العِلِّيَّةِ.

وَقَدْ تَقَرَّرَ فِي الأُصُولِ (عِلْمِ أُصُولِ الفِقْهِ)، فِي مَسْلَكِ الإيماءِ والتَّنْبِيهِ (وهو أحَدُ مسالِكِ استخراجِ العِلَّةِ، ويُقصَدُ بِهِ الدَّلالَةُ عَلى العِلِّيَّةِ بِالإشارَةِ والتَّنْبِيهِ)، أنَّ الفاءَ مِن حُرُوفِ التَّعْلِيلِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: سَهى فَسَجَدَ، وسَرَقَ فَقُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ، أيْ لِعِلَّةِ السَّهْوِ فِي الأوَّلِ، ولِعِلَّةِ السَّرِقَةِ فِي الثّانِي، وأُتْبِعَ ذَلِكَ بِالتَّهْدِيدِ لِمَنِ اتَّبَعَ الهَوى، فَأضَلَّهُ رَبُّنا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعالى بَعْدَهُ يَلِيهِ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِما نَسُوا يَوْمَ الحِسابِ﴾ [ص: ٢٦].

[p. 340] وَمَعْلُومٌ أنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ داوُدَ لا يَحْكُمُ بِغَيْرِ الحَقِّ، ولا يَتَّبِعُ الهَوى فَيُضِلَّهُ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى يَأْمُرُ أنْبِياءَهُ عَلَيْهِمُ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ ويَنْهاهُمْ لِيَشْرَعَ لِأُمَمِهِمْ.

وَلِذَلِكَ أمَرَ نَبِيَّنا ﷺ بِمِثْلِ ما أمَرَ بِهِ داوُدَ، ونَهاهُ أيْضًا عَنْ مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ، فِي آياتٍ مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ:

• كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَإنْ حَكَمْتَ فاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالقِسْطِ﴾ [الحجر: ٤٢].

• وَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ولا تَتَّبِعْ أهْواءَهُمْ واحْذَرْهُمْ أنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ عَنْ بَعْضِ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إلَيْكَ﴾ [الحجر: ٤٩].

• وَكَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا تُطِعِ الكافِرِينَ والمُنافِقِينَ﴾ [الأحزاب: ٤٨].

• وَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِمًا أوْ كَفُورًا﴾ [الإنسان: ٢٤].

• وَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ مَنْ أغْفَلْنا قَلْبَهُ عَنْ ذِكْرِنا واتَّبَعَ هَواهُ﴾ الآيَةَ [الكهف: ٢٨].

وَقَدْ قَدَّمْنا الكَلامَ عَلى هَذا فِي سُورَةِ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ، فِي الكَلامِ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿لا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَخْذُولًا﴾ [الإسراء: ٢٢].

وَبَيَّنّا أنَّ مِن أصْرَحِ الأدِلَّةِ القُرْآنِيَّةِ الدّالَّةِ عَلى أنَّ النَّبِيَّ يُخاطَبُ بِخِطابٍ، والمُرادُ بِذَلِكَ الخِطابِ غَيْرُهُ يَقِينًا، قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَقَضى رَبُّكَ ألّا تَعْبُدُوا إلّا إيّاهُ وبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا إمّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الكِبَرَ أحَدُهُما أوْ كِلاهُما فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ ولا تَنْهَرْهُما﴾ الآيَةَ [الإسراء: ٢٣]. ومِنَ المَعْلُومِ أنَّ أباهُ ﷺ تُوُفِّيَ قَبْلَ وِلادَتِهِ، وأنَّ أمَّهُ ماتَتْ وهُوَ صَغِيرٌ، ومَعَ ذَلِكَ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ يُخاطِبُهُ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إمّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الكِبَرَ أحَدُهُما أوْ كِلاهُما﴾، ومَعْلُومٌ أنَّهُ لا يَبْلُغُ عِنْدَهُ الكِبَرَ أحَدُهُما ولا كِلاهُما، لِأنَّهُما قَدْ ماتا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ بِزَمانٍ.

فَتَبَيَّنَ أنَّ أمْرَهُ تَعالى لِنَبِيِّهِ ونَهْيَهُ لَهُ فِي قَوْلِهِ ﴿فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ ولا تَنْهَرْهُما وقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا﴾ ﴿واخْفِضْ لَهُما جَناحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ﴾ الآيَةَ، إنَّما يُرادُ بِهِ التَّشْرِيعُ عَلى لِسانِهِ لِأُمَّتِهِ، ولا يُرادُ بِهِ هُوَ نَفْسُهُ ﷺ. وَقَدْ قَدَّمْنا هُناكَ أنَّ مِن أمْثالِ العَرَبِ: إيّاكَ أعْنِي واسْمَعِي يا جارَةُ، وذَكَرْنا فِي ذَلِكَ رَجَزَ سَهْلِ بْنِ مالِكٍ الفَزارِيِّ الَّذِي خاطَبَ بِهِ امْرَأةً، وهُوَ يَقْصِدُ أُخْرى، وهِيَ أُخْتُ حارِثَةَ بْنِ لَأْمٍ الطّائِيِّ، وهُوَ قَوْلُهُ:

يا أُخْتَ خَيْرِ البَدْوِ والحَضارَهْ ... كَيْفَ تَرَيْنَ فِي فَتى فَزارَهْ

أصْبَحَ يَهْوى حُرَّةً مِعْطارَهْ ∗∗∗ إيّاكِ أعْنِي واسْمَعِي يا جارَهْ

وَذَكَرْنا هُناكَ الرَّجَزَ الَّذِي أجابَتْهُ بِهِ المَرْأةُ، وقَوْلَ بَعْضِ أهْلِ العِلْمِ: إنَّ الخِطابَ فِي [p. 341] قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إمّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الكِبَرَ أحَدُهُما أوْ كِلاهُما﴾ الآيَةَ، هُوَ الخِطابُ بِصِيغَةِ المُفْرَدِ، الَّذِي يُرادُ بِهِ عُمُومُ كُلِّ مَن يَصِحُّ خِطابُهُ، كَقَوْلِ طَرَفَةَ بْنِ العَبْدِ فِي مُعَلَّقَتِهِ:

سَتُبْدِي لَكَ الأيّامُ ما كُنْتَ جاهِلًا ∗∗∗ ويَأْتِيكَ بِالأخْبارِ مَن لَمْ تُزَوِّدِ

أيْ: سَتُبْدِي لَكَ ويَأْتِيكَ أيُّها الإنْسانُ الَّذِي يَصِحُّ خِطابُكَ. وعَلى هَذا فَلا دَلِيلَ فِي الآيَةِ، وهُوَ قَوْلٌ غَيْرُ صَحِيحٍ. وفِي سِياقِ الآياتِ قَرِينَةٌ قُرْآنِيَّةٌ واضِحَةٌ دالَّةٌ عَلى أنَّ المُخاطَبَ بِذَلِكَ هُوَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ، وعَلَيْهِ فالِاسْتِدْلالُ بِالآيَةِ اسْتِدْلالٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ صَحِيحٌ. والقَرِينَةُ القُرْآنِيَّةُ المَذْكُورَةُ هِيَ أنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ فِي تِلْكَ الأوامِرِ والنَّواهِي الَّتِي خاطَبَ بِها رَسُولَهُ ﷺ، الَّتِي أوَّلُها: ﴿وَبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا إمّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الكِبَرَ﴾ الآيَةَ، ما هُوَ صَرِيحٌ فِي أنَّ المُخاطَبَ بِذَلِكَ هُوَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ، لا عُمُومُ كُلِّ مَن يَصِحُّ مِنْهُ الخِطابُ، وذَلِكَ فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ذَلِكَ مِمّا أوْحى إلَيْكَ رَبُّكَ مِنَ الحِكْمَةِ ولا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ فَتُلْقى فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَدْحُورًا﴾ [الإسراء: ٣٩].

(p-342) Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in the end of Surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 85], and at the end of Surah al-Mu'minun, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose...﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115].

* *

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieved, so woe to those who disbelieved from the Fire﴾. The demonstrative in His saying "that" (dhalika) refers to the verbal noun (al-masdar) contained within the "artificial verb" (al-fi'l al-sina'i, the grammatical verb form, as distinguished from the actual event). Thus, "that," i.e., creating the heavens and the earth in vain, is the assumption of those who disbelieved in Us. The negation in His saying "We did not create" applies to the state (al-hal), not to its governing verb, which is "We created," because what is negated by the negative particle "ma" is not His creating the heavens and the earth, which is affirmed; rather, what is negated by it is that it was "in vain." Therefore, it is a state that is nearly a principal element (hal shibh al-'umdah), not a plain accusative complement (fadlah sarihah), since the negation applies to it alone, and the sentence is not valid without it. The discussion of this is well known in its own place. The negation that His creating the heavens and the earth was in vain is something He declared Himself free of, and His righteous servants also declare Him free of it, because it does not befit His perfection and majesty, exalted is He.

As for His declaring Himself free of it, it is in His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115].

(p-343) Then He declared Himself free, from the notion that He created them in vain, by His saying: ﴿Exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth. There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 116], i.e., He is exalted, sanctified, and declared free of having created them in vain.

As for His righteous servants declaring Him free of that, it is in His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding. Who remember Allah standing and sitting and on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; exalted are You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾. His saying about them, "Exalted are You," means: [it is] a declaration of Your freedom from being such that You created the heavens and the earth in vain. Their saying "Exalted are You" is a declaration of His freedom, just as He declared Himself free of that by His saying: ﴿Exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 116], and so on.

His saying in this verse: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieved from the Fire﴾ indicates that whoever ascribes to Allah, majestic and exalted is He, what does not befit Him, for him is the Fire.

Allah has also made clear in another place that whoever ascribes to Allah what does not befit Him, it has ruined him, made him among the losers, and made the Fire his abode. This is in His saying: ﴿But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do. And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has ruined you, and you have become among the losers. So if they endure, the Fire is their residence﴾ [Fussilat: 22–24].

Our statement at the beginning of this discussion, that the demonstrative in His saying "that" refers to the verbal noun contained in the artificial verb, we have already clarified in Surah al-Isra', in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9]. There we explained that the verb has two types: the actual verb (al-fi'l al-haqiqi), and the artificial verb (al-fi'l al-sina'i). As for the actual verb, it is the occurring event, known among the grammarians as the verbal noun (al-masdar).

As for the artificial verb, it is what is known in the discipline of grammar as the past verb, the present verb, and the imperative verb, according to the view that the imperative is independent of the present.

It is known that the artificial verb, according to the grammarians, resolves into a verbal noun and a tense, as indicated in the Khulasah [of Ibn Malik] by his saying:

(p-344) "The verbal noun is the name of what, other than time, is among the connoted meanings of the verb, like amn from amina."

According to groups of the rhetoricians, it resolves into a verbal noun, a tense, and an attribution (nisbah), and this is the closer view, as some scholars of rhetoric have set forth in the discussion of the metaphor of the sequential type (al-isti'arah al-tab'iyyah). From this you know that there is no disagreement among them that the verbal noun and the tense are both contained in the artificial verb, so it is valid for the demonstrative and the pronoun to refer to either the verbal noun or the tense contained in the artificial verb.

An example of the demonstrative referring to the verbal noun contained in the verb is His saying here: ﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieved﴾, and so on. The verbal noun, which is the creating, is contained in the artificial verb, which is the past verb in His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That﴾, i.e., the creating of the heavens mentioned, which is contained in the concept of "We created," is the assumption of those who disbelieved.

An example of the demonstrative referring to the tense contained in the concept of the artificial verb is His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown; that is the Day of the Promised Punishment﴾ [Qaf: 20], i.e., that time contained in the verb is the Day of the Promised Punishment.

An example of the pronoun referring to the verbal noun contained in the concept of the verb is His saying: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 8]. So His saying "that" (huwa) refers to justice (al-'adl), which is contained in the concept of "be just" (i'dilu), as has already been clarified.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on the earth? Or shall We make the righteous like the wicked?﴾ The particle "am" (أم) in His saying "am naj'alu alladhina" and in His saying "am naj'alu al-muttaqin," both of them, is a disjunctive "am" (munqati'a), and the disjunctive "am" has three positions among the scholars of Arabic grammar:

The first: that it has the meaning of the interrogative hamzah of denial (hamzat istifham al-inkar).

The second: that it has the meaning of "bal" (rather), the particle of transition (al-idrab).

The third: that it includes the meaning of denial and of transition together, and this is the view chosen by some of the researchers (al-muhaqqiqin).

Accordingly, the transition (al-idrab) made by it here is a transition from one point to another (intiqali), not a cancellation (ibtali). The reason for the denial directed at them by it is clear, because whoever thinks of Allah, the All-Wise, the All-Aware, that He treats the righteous reformer and the corrupt wicked person as equal, has held an ugly opinion deserving of denial.

Allah, may He be majestic and exalted, has explained this meaning in another place besides this one, and condemned the judgement of whoever judges by it, in His saying in Surah al-Jathiyah: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is that which they judge.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21]

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 29:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses and that people of understanding may take heed.﴾ His saying, may He be exalted: *kitābun* ("a Book") is the predicate (*khabar*) of an omitted subject (*mubtada'*), i.e., "this is a Book." In this noble verse, He, may He be exalted, has mentioned that He sent down this Book, magnifying Himself, may He be exalted, by using the plural form; that it is a blessed Book; and that among the wisdom of its revelation is that people should reflect upon its verses (*yatadabbarū*), meaning that they should understand them, consider them, and examine them closely, until they grasp the kinds of guidance contained therein; and that people of understanding (*ulū al-albāb*) should take heed, meaning that those with sound intellects, free from the flaws of deficiency, should be admonished.

Everything He mentioned in this noble verse has been made clear in other verses.

As for His, may He be exalted, being the One who sent down this Qur'an, He has mentioned it in many verses, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ [al-Qadr: 1]

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down in a blessed night﴾ [al-Dukhān: 3]

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are definitive, they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are ambiguous﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 7].

Verses similar to these are many and well known.

As for this Book being blessed, He has mentioned it in verses of His Book, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, confirming that which came before it﴾ [al-Anʿām: 92], and the verse continues. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and fear God, that you may receive mercy﴾ [al-Anʿām: 155]. The *mubārak* (blessed) is one abundant in blessings, of the good of this world and the Hereafter.

We ask God, the Near, the Responder, since He has granted us success in serving this blessed Book, to make us blessed wherever we are, to bless us and to bless through us, to encompass us with His great blessings in this world and the Hereafter, and to extend them to all our Muslim brothers who act upon His commands with blessings and goodness, in this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, He is Near and Responsive.

[p-345] As for the reflection upon its verses being among the wisdoms of its revelation, He has alluded to it in some verses, by urging reflection upon it and rebuking those who do not reflect upon it, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muḥammad: 24].

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than God, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 82].

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not reflected upon the word, or has there come to them that which did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 68].

As for the taking heed of people of understanding being among the wisdoms of its revelation, He has mentioned it in other than this place, combined with some other wisdoms not mentioned in the verse of (Ṣ) here. Such as His saying, may He be exalted, in Surah Ibrāhīm: ﴿This is a message for mankind, that they may be warned by it, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that people of understanding may take heed﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 52]. In this noble verse He has made clear that the taking heed of people of understanding is among the wisdoms of its revelation, specifying from it two other wisdoms: warning people by it, and realizing the meaning of *lā ilāha illā Allāh* (there is no god but God). That warning people and the taking heed of people of understanding are among the wisdoms of its revelation is mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lām, Mīm, Ṣād. A Book revealed to you, so let there be no constriction in your breast concerning it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 1-2]. This is because the lām in His saying "that you may warn" (*li-tundhira*) is connected to His saying "revealed" (*unzila*), and *al-dhikrā* (reminder) is a verbal noun (*ism maṣdar*) meaning *al-tadhkīr* (admonition). And the believers in the verse, it is not hidden, are the people of understanding.

The mention of the wisdom of warning appears in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqān: 1].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whomever it reaches﴾ [al-Anʿām: 19].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿A revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful, that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾ [Yā Sīn: 5-6], and the verse continues.

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That it may warn whoever is alive﴾ [Yā Sīn: 70], and the verse continues.

It is mentioned in other verses that among the wisdoms of its revelation is both warning and giving glad tidings together, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue only that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people﴾ [Maryam: 97]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Praise be to God, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance, [but made it] straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Kahf: 1-2], and the verse continues.

He, may He be exalted, has made clear that among the wisdoms of its revelation is that the Messenger (ﷺ) should explain to people what was sent down to them, and in order that they may give thought. That is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may make clear to people what has been sent down to them, and perhaps they will give thought﴾ [al-Naḥl: 44].

[p-346] We have previously mentioned several times that *laʿalla* (perhaps) is among the particles of causation (*ḥurūf al-taʿlīl*), and the wisdom of explanation mentioned here is accompanied by the wisdom of guidance and mercy in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that over which they differ, and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [al-Naḥl: 64].

He has made clear that among the wisdoms of its revelation is the firming of the believers, and guidance and glad tidings for the Muslims, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to strengthen those who believe, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims"﴾ [al-Naḥl: 102].

He has made clear that among the wisdoms of its revelation, sent to the Prophet (ﷺ), is that he should judge between people by what God has shown him. That is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 105].

The apparent meaning of His saying: ﴿by that which God has shown you﴾ is by that which He has taught you of the knowledge in this great Qur'an, as evidenced by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an inspiration of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was], but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [al-Shūrā: 52], the verse continues. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an, although before it you were among the unaware﴾ [Yūsuf: 3].

He, may He be exalted, has made clear that among the wisdoms of its revelation is bringing people out of darknesses into light, and that is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lām, Rā. A Book which We have sent down to you that you may bring mankind out of darkness into light, by the permission of their Lord﴾, the verse continues [Ibrāhīm: 1].

He has made clear that among the wisdoms of its revelation is a reminder for whoever fears, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Ṭā Hā. We have not sent down to you the Qur'an that you be distressed, but only as a reminder for those who fear﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 1-3], meaning: We have not sent it down except as a reminder for whoever fears.

This restriction to reminder is relative (*idāfī*), and likewise the restriction in His saying, may He be exalted, which we mentioned before this: ﴿And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that over which they differ﴾, the verse continues [al-Naḥl: 64], by the evidence of the other wisdoms we have mentioned.

He has made clear that among the wisdoms of its revelation, as an Arabic Qur'an, and of God's varying of threats within it, is that people may fear God, or that this Book may produce for them a remembrance, meaning an admonition and a reminder that guides them to the truth. That is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, and We have varied in it some of the warnings, that perhaps they may fear God, or it may produce for them a remembrance﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 113]. And God, may He be exalted, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We bestowed upon Dawud Sulayman﴾. In this noble verse He mentions that He gave Sulayman to Dawud (as a gift). He has explained in Surat an-Naml that the one who was given (as a gift) inherited from the one to whom he was given, and that is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Sulayman inherited from Dawud﴾ [an-Naml: 16].

We have also explained in Surat Maryam, in discussing His saying, exalted is He, concerning Zakariyya: ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾ [Maryam: 5-6], that it is an inheritance of knowledge and religion, not an inheritance of wealth.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did try Solomon and placed upon his throne a body﴾. We have already presented the discussion of this verse, and of what the exegetes mention concerning it from the narrations whose weakness is not hidden, and that they are not fitting for the station of prophethood, in surah al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," ﴾ ﴿except [adding], "If Allah wills."﴾ [al-Kahf: 23-24]. And what has been related from the early generations (al-salaf) from among those narrations, that the devil took Solomon's ring, sat on his throne, and drove Solomon away, and so on to its end, is shown to be false by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you among the deviators﴾ [al-Hijr: 42], and by the devil's acknowledgment of this in His saying: ﴿except Your chosen servants among them﴾ [al-Hijr: 40].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 36:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We subjected the wind to him, blowing gently by his command, wherever he directed.﴾ We have already presented the discussion of this verse, clarified with Qur'anic verses, in Surat al-Anbiya' in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, violent, running by his command﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:81], and so on.

There we explained His saying here, ﴿wherever he directed﴾ (ḥaythu aṣāba, lit. "where he struck"), and we mentioned there the ways of reconciling His saying here, "gently" (rukhā'an), with His saying there, ﴿violent﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:81]. Also, the way of reconciling the generality of directions understood from His saying here, ﴿wherever he directed⁠﴾ (i.e., wherever he willed), with the particularity of the blessed land mentioned there in His saying, ﴿running by his command to the land which We had blessed﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:81], and so on.

(p-348) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾. We have already explained this with Qur'anic verses in Surah al-Anbiya' in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And of the devils were those who dove for him and performed other work besides that, and We were watching over them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 82].

Allah's statement: ﴿And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."﴾ up to His statement ﴿as a reminder for those of understanding.﴾ We have already set forth its clarification by means of the Qur'anic verses, along with addressing the removal of what it contains of difficulty, in Surah al-Anbiya' in the discussion of His statement, ﴿And Job, when he called to his Lord﴾ up to His statement: ﴿and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham and Isaac﴾. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet ﷺ in this noble verse to mention His servant Abraham, and He did not restrict that remembrance by it being in the Book (al-Kitab), even though He restricted it by that in Surah Maryam, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham; indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 41].

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And remember Ismail and al-Yasa'﴾. Here too he issued the command to mention Ismail without restriction, whereas in Surah Maryam he restricted it by his being in the Book, in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Ismail; indeed he was true to his promise﴾ [Maryam: 54] and so on. This indicates that he (ﷺ) is likewise commanded to mention all of those who are mentioned in the Book. For this reason, the mention of all of them has come in the Noble Qur'an, as is well known.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿And with them are those restricting their gaze, [and] equal in age﴾. We have already discussed this in Surah As-Saffat, in the discussion of Allah's saying: ﴿And with them are those restricting their gaze, with beautiful, wide eyes﴾ [As-Saffat: 48].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no depletion.﴾ What this noble verse contains, namely that the bliss of Paradise has no nafad (exhaustion or ending) for it, meaning it has no cessation and no cessation of existence, He mentioned in other verses, such as His saying concerning it: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾ [Hud: 108], and His saying: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, but what is with Allah is enduring﴾ [An-Nahl: 96].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is the truth: the mutual disputing of the people of the Fire.﴾ We have already presented what clarifies this from the Qur'anic verses in several places of this blessed Book. We mentioned some of them in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166], and we mentioned some of it in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein﴾ [al-A'raf: 38], and other than that from the (other) places.

Allah's statement: ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾

This has already been explained, along with some related discussions, in Surat al-Baqarah, in the commentary on His statement: ﴿Except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34]

Allah says: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Hud, and we mentioned the rulings related to these verses in the discussion of His statement, exalted is He, about His prophet Nuh: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth for it; my reward is only from Allah﴾ [Hud: 29], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 88:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you will surely come to know its news after a time.﴾ Regarding the "time" (ḥīn) mentioned here, some scholars said: what is meant by it is after death, and what supports this is what we previously presented in Surat al-Ḥijr, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty.﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 99].

And some scholars said: the "time" mentioned here is the Day of Resurrection, and there is no contradiction between the two statements, because after death the realities of guidance and misguidance become clear to a person.

The lām in "litaʿlamunna" (lataʿlamunna) is the lām that prepares for an oath (lām al-muwaṭṭiʾah lil-qasam), and in this noble verse He has emphasized, through the oath and the emphatic nūn (nūn al-tawkīd), that they will surely come to know the news of the Qur'an, i.e., its truthfulness and the correctness of everything in it, after a time.

As for what this noble verse includes of a threat to the disbelievers that they will come to know its news after a time, He, may He be exalted, has already alluded to it in Surat al-Anʿam, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But your people have denied it, while it is the truth. Say, "I am not over you a guardian."﴾ ﴿For every news is a fixed time, and you will come to know.﴾ [al-Anʿam: 66–67].

(p-350) Many scholars said: ﴿For every news is a fixed time﴾ means: for every report there is a reality and an occurrence. If it is true, its truthfulness becomes evident, even if after a time; and if it is false, its falsehood becomes evident. And you will come to know the truth of this Qur'an, even if after a time.
